verdicts.rule: [1] There are exactly FOUR exit-code classes. (1) exit 0 = full 12-line success, or -h/--help. (2) exit 2 = any argparse failure: stderr is exactly two lines, `usage: <prog> [-h] --a A --b B --c C --d D --e E --f F --g G\n<prog>: error: <msg>\n`, and NO `[PYI-...]` line. (3) exit 1 = any uncaught Python exception from the 12 computation statements: stderr is a traceback followed by a `[PYI-<pid>:ERROR] ...` line. (4) NO EXIT AT ALL (infinite loop, must be killed) when --f or --g is negative.
verdicts.counterexample:
THREE independent counterexamples.

(A) exit-2 stderr is NOT always two lines. The 'unrecognized arguments' message interpolates argv VERBATIM (no repr), so a newline in an unknown token splits the line:
$ /workspace/dataset/test20_executable --a x --b 2 --c x --d y --e 3 --f 1 --g 2 --q $'1\n2'

usage: test20_executable [-h] --a A --b B --c C --d D --e E --f F --g G$
test20_executable: error: unrecognized arguments: --q 1$
2$

$ COLUMNS=30 /workspace/dataset/test20_executable --f zz
RC=2, stderr = 5 lines:

       C --d D --e E --f F$
